title.value: The Topic Confusion Task: A Novel Evaluation Scenario for Authorship Attribution
title.justification: The title is clearly mentioned at the beginning of the document.
title.quote: The Topic Confusion Task: A Novel Evaluation Scenario for Authorship Attribution

analysis.description: The paper introduces a new evaluation scenario for authorship attribution called the 'topic confusion task,' which aims to better discern the influence of topic shifts versus writing style capture in authorship attribution errors. It examines how different features used in authorship attribution respond to topic changes by proposing a controlled switching of topics associated with authors between training and testing phases. It finds that word-level n-grams outperform language models like BERT and RoBERTa for this task and contributes a curated dataset to facilitate future research.

type.justification: The paper reports on experimental results from authorship attribution models applied to new evaluation settings, demonstrating performance differences and analyzing error types.
type.quote: We show that stylo-metric features with part-of-speech tags are the least susceptible to topic variations. We further show that combining them with other features leads to significantly lower topic confusion and higher attribution accuracy.
